svg.title: Three-point estimate and the normal curve
svg.desc: Optimistic 6, most likely 9, pessimistic 18 days give a triangular estimate of 11 and a PERT estimate of 10 with a standard deviation of 2. The normal curve shows that about 68.27 percent of outcomes fall within one standard deviation (8 to 12 days), 95.45 percent within two (6 to 14) and 99.73 percent within three (4 to 16). The same bands set control chart limits at the mean plus or minus three sigma.
svg.text: Three-point estimates and the normal curve
PERT example: O = 6, M = 9, P = 18 days → expected 10 days, standard deviation 2 days
Project: add the expected durations on the critical path;
Control chart limits = mean ± 3σ (in control inside them)
Seven points in a row on one side of the mean signal a
Six Sigma target: 3.4 defects per million
Example for a path of three activities with variances 4, 9 and 2.25: total variance 15.25, SD ≈ 3.9 days. There is about a 68% chance that the path finishes within plus or minus
one SD of its summed expected duration.
